source: Master Specification v1.0 + DATABASE-PROVIDER-POLICY.md + Backlog v1.0

rules.title: EF Core Code First — Provider-Neutral Domain
rules.statement: VetFlow uses EF Core Code First. Domain and application layers must remain database-provider independent. No provider-specific business logic is permitted.
rules.rationale: Supports SQLite locally and PostgreSQL in production without code changes in domain/application layers.

rules.title: SQLite — Local Development Only
rules.statement: SQLite is the default database for local developer machines only. SQLite-specific behavior must not enter business logic. SQLite passing alone does not establish production compatibility.
rules.rationale: Resource-efficient local dev without requiring a database server.

rules.title: PostgreSQL — Canonical CI/Staging/Production Provider
rules.statement: PostgreSQL is the canonical provider for CI, staging, and production. Persistence-related stories require PostgreSQL validation before completion.
rules.rationale: Architectural truth. Database-per-tenant architecture must remain intact.

rules.title: Explicit EF Core Configuration
rules.statement: Important keys, relationships, constraints, indexes, and precision must be explicitly configured in EF Core. Do not rely on convention-only configuration for business-critical constraints.
rules.rationale: Ensures correct schema across both SQLite and PostgreSQL providers.

rules.title: Database Migrations Are Version-Controlled
rules.statement: All EF Core migrations must be committed to version control. Migrations are never applied by bypassing EF Core tooling.
rules.rationale: Ensures reproducible schema evolution across all environments.

rules.title: Tenant Resolution From Trusted Identity Only
rules.statement: Tenant context must be resolved from the authenticated identity (Keycloak JWT claims) only. Never accept an arbitrary browser-supplied tenant ID as authoritative.

rules.title: Server-Side Authorization — Frontend Guards Are UX Only
rules.statement: All authorization decisions must be enforced server-side. Angular route guards and permission directives are UX convenience only and must not substitute for API authorization.
rules.rationale: Frontend code is not a trust boundary.

rules.title: AI Not in V1 Transactional Path
rules.statement: AI suggestions must not directly finalize clinical records. Human acceptance is required for any AI-generated content. AI must not bypass normal authorization.

rules.source: Backlog v1.0 — Standard Antigravity Execution Contract
rules.title: Antigravity Execution Contract — No Unrelated Scope
rules.statement: During implementation, edits must be restricted strictly to the tasks and files specified in the story. Do not modify unrelated scope, perform speculative refactoring, or introduce unplanned abstractions.
rules.rationale: Maintains story-by-story traceability and prevents scope drift.

rules.title: Avoid Over-DRY and Speculative Abstractions
rules.statement: Do not extract business logic into shared generic components prematurely. Business-specific document composition, workflow logic, and domain rules must remain in their own vertical slices. DRY applies to stable infrastructure primitives only.
rules.rationale: Prevents hidden coupling across business workflows. Follows vertical slice architecture.

rules.title: Run Build and Tests — Provide Evidence
rules.statement: Every story implementation must run build and tests and provide concrete evidence (build output, test results, migration output) before moving to Verification.

rules.title: Zero Secret Storage
rules.statement: Never write raw credentials, PATs, API keys, or passwords into .devweave/, source code, configuration files, or Git history. Use environment variables or secret managers.

rules.title: Open-Source-First
rules.statement: Prefer open-source libraries and tools. Do not introduce commercial/proprietary dependencies without an explicit Architecture Decision Record (ADR) and developer approval.
rules.rationale: Cost efficiency and vendor independence for SaaS.
